## Why this package exists

Australia, New Zealand and China kept strict border quarantine in place for
most of the pandemic. The United Kingdom, the United States and Sweden did
not. Asking which approach did better sounds like a question with one answer.
It is not, and that is what this package is built to show.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-ishamantri")
```

```{r setup}
library(bordercovid)
```

## The data

`covid_border` holds daily case and death rates per million for the six
countries, from March 2020 to December 2023.

```{r}
head(covid_border)
```

Rates are per million and smoothed over seven days, so countries of very
different sizes can sit on the same axis and weekend reporting gaps do not
show up as spikes.

## Summarising a period

`summarise_period()` takes any two dates and returns one row per country,
sorted by deaths over the window.

```{r}
summarise_period()
```

Over the whole period the two groups are hard to separate. Now narrow it to
the first year.

```{r}
summarise_period(from = "2020-03-01", to = "2020-12-31")
```

The gap is enormous. New Zealand averaged around one case per million a day
while the United Kingdom averaged over a hundred.

Now take 2022 on its own.

```{r}
summarise_period(from = "2022-01-01", to = "2022-12-31")
```

The ranking inverts. Australia and New Zealand record the highest mean case
rates of all six countries.

## What that means

Strict border control did not stop the wave, it moved it. Those countries
delayed their first large outbreak until vaccination coverage was high, which
is why their death totals stay low even in the window where their case rates
are highest. Reading a single window and calling it the answer gets it wrong
in one direction or the other.

## Exploring it directly

```r
run_app()
```

The app has a date range, a choice of cases or deaths, and country
checkboxes. Moving the date range is the thing worth doing: the plot, the
table and the written reading underneath all update together, and the verdict
at the top reverses between the 2020 and 2022 windows.
